title: Jonah Chapter 2 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jonah chapter 2 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jonah Chapter 2 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jonah Chapter 2.

questions.question: Where was Jonah when he prayed to the LORD his God?
questions.correctAnswer: Out of the fish's belly
questions.explanation: Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly, as stated in Jonah 2:1.

questions.question: According to Jonah 2, why did Jonah cry unto the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Because of his affliction
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'I cried by reason of mine affliction unto the LORD,' in Jonah 2:2.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah said that the LORD heard his voice when he cried out from the belly of hell.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'out of the belly of hell cried I, and thou heardest my voice,' showing that the LORD heard him (Jonah 2:2).

questions.question: What had God done to Jonah according to Jonah 2:3?
options: Cast him into the deep in the seas
questions.correctAnswer: Cast him into the deep in the seas
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'For thou hadst cast me into the deep, in the midst of the seas,' as recorded in Jonah 2:3.

questions.question: True or False: The floods and waves passed over Jonah while he was in the deep sea.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah stated that 'the floods compassed me about: all thy billows and thy waves passed over me' in Jonah 2:3.

questions.question: What did Jonah say he would do despite feeling cast out of God's sight?
options: Look again toward thy holy temple
questions.correctAnswer: Look again toward thy holy temple
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple,' as found in Jonah 2:4.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah prayed to the LORD when his soul fainted within him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse stating Jonah prayed when his soul fainted is Jonah 2:7, not covered in the early verses focused on here.

questions.question: Which of the following did Jonah mention as surrounding him in the deep waters?
questions.correctAnswer: Weeds wrapped about his head
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'the weeds were wrapped about my head,' as described in Jonah 2:5.

questions.question: What did Jonah say was about him 'for ever' when he went down to the bottoms of the mountains?
questions.correctAnswer: The earth with her bars
questions.explanation: Jonah stated, 'the earth with her bars was about me for ever,' in Jonah 2:6.

questions.question: Which phrase best describes Jonah's prayer coming to God according to Jonah 2?
questions.correctAnswer: Into thine holy temple
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple,' as found in Jonah 2:7.

questions.question: In Jonah 2, which action happened first?
options: Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly
The LORD spake unto the fish to vomit Jonah out
Jonah said he would sacrifice with thanksgiving
Jonah remembered the LORD when his soul fainted
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah prayed unto the LORD his God out of the fish's belly
questions.explanation: Jonah's prayer in the fish's belly is the opening event in Jonah 2:1, occurring before the fish vomited him out (2:10) or other events.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah said that salvation is of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah declared, 'Salvation is of the LORD,' in Jonah 2:9.

questions.question: What did the LORD command the fish to do in Jonah 2?
options: Vomit Jonah upon the dry land
questions.correctAnswer: Vomit Jonah upon the dry land
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:10 says, 'the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.'

questions.question: According to Jonah 2, what do those who observe lying vanities do?
questions.correctAnswer: Forsake their own mercy
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:8 states, 'They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy.'

questions.question: What did Jonah vow to pay with the voice of thanksgiving?
questions.correctAnswer: That which he vowed
questions.explanation: Jonah said, 'I will pay that that I have vowed,' in Jonah 2:9.

medium.title: Jonah Chapter 2 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jonah Chapter 2 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jonah 2:5, what surrounded Jonah even to his soul?
questions.correctAnswer: The waters
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:5 states that 'The waters compassed me about, even to the soul,' indicating that the waters surrounded Jonah deeply.

questions.question: How does Jonah 2:6 describe the earth in relation to Jonah's predicament?
options: The earth embraced him with open arms
The earth with her bars was about him forever
The earth shook beneath his feet
questions.correctAnswer: The earth with her bars was about him forever
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:6 says, 'the earth with her bars was about me for ever,' describing the earth as imprisoning him in his distress.

questions.question: What action did Jonah take when his soul fainted, according to Jonah 2:7?
options: He remembered the LORD and prayed
questions.correctAnswer: He remembered the LORD and prayed
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 clearly states, 'When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee,' showing Jonah's reliance on prayer in hardship.

questions.question: What does Jonah 2:8 warn about those who observe lying vanities?
questions.correctAnswer: They forsake their own mercy
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:8 says, 'They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy,' teaching the consequence of trusting falsehoods instead of God.

questions.question: What does Jonah 2:9 indicate about the source of salvation?
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is from the LORD
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 states, 'Salvation is of the LORD,' emphasizing that deliverance comes solely from God.

questions.question: How does Jonah 2:5-6 illustrate the depth of Jonah's distress and God's deliverance?
options: Jonah was surrounded by water and earth's bars, yet God saved him from corruption
Jonah was on dry land and surrounded by mountains, without hope
Jonah was lost in the desert but found shelter
Jonah was imprisoned by men but escaped by his own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Jonah was surrounded by water and earth's bars, yet God saved him from corruption
questions.explanation: Verses 5 and 6 describe Jonah enclosed by waters and earth's bars, representing his dire situation, but also affirm that God 'brought up my life from corruption,' showing divine rescue.

questions.question: Based on Jonah 2:7 and 2:8, what happens when one remembers the LORD and prays compared to observing lying vanities?
options: Remembering the LORD leads to prayer being heard, while observing vanities results in forsaking mercy
Observing vanities brings mercy, remembering the LORD leads to despair
Neither action affects mercy or prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering the LORD leads to prayer being heard, while observing vanities results in forsaking mercy
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 shows prayer reaching God's temple when Jonah remembers Him, whereas 2:8 warns that those who follow falsehoods forsake their mercy, contrasting faith with false trust.

questions.question: What biblical principle about prayer and remembrance of God can be drawn from Jonah 2:7?
options: Prayer is effective when one remembers God in times of weakness
Prayer has no effect regardless of remembrance
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer is effective when one remembers God in times of weakness
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 highlights that when Jonah's soul fainted, he remembered God, and his prayer entered God's holy temple, teaching the importance of recalling God in hardship.

questions.question: A fellow believer feels overwhelmed by difficulties and doubts God's mercy. Based on Jonah 2:5-8, what truth might encourage them?
options: Even when surrounded by troubles like waters and earth's bars, remembering God and praying brings mercy and salvation
Difficulties mean God has forsaken them
Mercy is lost when troubles come
Only observing vanities will bring relief
questions.correctAnswer: Even when surrounded by troubles like waters and earth's bars, remembering God and praying brings mercy and salvation
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:5-8 teaches that despite being overwhelmed, Jonah's remembrance of God and prayer led to mercy and salvation, showing that trust in God is essential in trials.

questions.question: What does Jonah 2:6 suggest about God's power over death and corruption?
options: God can bring life up from corruption
God has no control over death
Corruption is inevitable without human effort
questions.correctAnswer: God can bring life up from corruption
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:6 says, 'yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption,' indicating God's power to rescue life from death and decay.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah 2:8 teaches that those who trust in false things maintain their own mercy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:8 states, 'They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy,' meaning trusting falsehood causes loss of mercy.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jonah 2:9, thanksgiving and fulfilling vows are proper responses to God's salvation.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 expresses, 'But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed,' showing gratitude and integrity as responses to salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah 2:7 indicates that when Jonah's soul fainted, he forgot the LORD and stopped praying.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 explicitly says, 'When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee,' showing remembrance and continued prayer despite fainting.

questions.question: How does Jonah 2:5-7 teach about the relationship between affliction and spiritual focus?
options: Affliction draws the soul to remember and pray to God, even in deep distress
Affliction causes complete spiritual despair with no hope
Affliction is unrelated to spiritual focus
questions.correctAnswer: Affliction draws the soul to remember and pray to God, even in deep distress
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:5-7 shows that despite overwhelming waters and seeming confinement, Jonah's soul remembered the LORD and his prayer reached God, teaching that trials can deepen faith.

questions.question: What lesson about integrity can be drawn from Jonah 2:9 in the context of salvation?
options: One should faithfully fulfill vows made to God as part of thanksgiving for salvation
Vows are optional and not important
Salvation requires no response from the believer
Thanksgiving and vows are only for priests
questions.correctAnswer: One should faithfully fulfill vows made to God as part of thanksgiving for salvation
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 says, 'I will pay that that I have vowed,' highlighting the importance of integrity and gratitude following God's deliverance.

hard.title: Jonah Chapter 2 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jonah Chapter 2.

questions.question: According to Jonah 2:9, what is the source of salvation?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Jonah explicitly states in Jonah 2:9 that 'Salvation is of the LORD,' emphasizing that salvation comes solely from God.

questions.question: What action did Jonah vow to do as a form of thanksgiving according to Jonah 2:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifice unto God
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 states, 'But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed,' showing Jonah's commitment to offer sacrifices.

questions.question: What was the LORD's command to the fish in Jonah 2:10?
options: To vomit Jonah upon the dry land
questions.correctAnswer: To vomit Jonah upon the dry land
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:10 states, 'And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land,' showing God's control over the situation.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes Jonah’s statement in Jonah 2:9 about salvation coming from the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 3:8
questions.explanation: Psalm 3:8 states, 'Salvation belongeth unto the LORD,' echoing Jonah 2:9’s declaration that salvation is from the LORD.

questions.question: In Jonah 2:7, what brought Jonah’s prayer to God’s holy temple?
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering the LORD
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 states, 'When my soul fainted within me I remembered the LORD: and my prayer came in unto thee, into thine holy temple,' showing remembrance as the trigger for prayer.

questions.question: What literary device is exemplified in Jonah 2 by Jonah’s prayer starting in the depths and ending with praise and deliverance?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Jonah 2’s structure, moving from distress in the depths to deliverance and praise, forms a chiasm, a literary device where themes mirror around a central point.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the belly of hell' in Jonah 2:2 most likely signify in the Hebrew context?
options: The place of extreme distress or Sheol
questions.correctAnswer: The place of extreme distress or Sheol
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term behind 'belly of hell' often refers to Sheol, the realm of the dead, symbolizing Jonah’s intense affliction as per Jonah 2:2.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage references Jonah’s time in the fish as a foreshadowing of Christ’s resurrection?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 12:40
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:40 explicitly cites Jonah’s three days in the fish as a typology of Jesus’ death and resurrection, connecting to Jonah 2:10.

questions.question: In Jonah 2:8, what is the consequence of observing 'lying vanities'?
questions.correctAnswer: Forsaking their own mercy
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:8 says, 'They that observe lying vanities forsake their own mercy,' warning that false worship leads to loss of mercy.

questions.question: True or False: Jonah’s prayer in chapter 2 includes a vow to pay what he has promised to God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 states, 'I will pay that that I have vowed,' indicating Jonah’s commitment to fulfill his promises to God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Jonah 2:6, Jonah believed he was permanently trapped in the earth's bars and could not be rescued.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:6 says, 'the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption,' indicating Jonah believed God rescued him despite the seeming permanence.

questions.question: Which theme from Jonah 2 is prominently fulfilled in the book of Psalms?
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer for deliverance from distress
questions.explanation: Jonah’s prayer in distress (Jonah 2) echoes the psalms such as Psalm 42 and 69, where the psalmist cries out for God’s rescue.

questions.question: What does the imagery of 'weeds were wrapped about my head' in Jonah 2:5 symbolize?
options: Being overwhelmed and trapped by distress
questions.correctAnswer: Being overwhelmed and trapped by distress
questions.explanation: The weeds around Jonah’s head in Jonah 2:5 symbolize being entangled and overwhelmed by the depths, emphasizing his dire situation.

questions.question: How does Jonah 2:4 show a turning point in Jonah’s attitude during his prayer?
options: He moves from despair to hope by turning his eyes toward God’s temple
He curses God for his punishment
He asks the fish to rescue him
questions.correctAnswer: He moves from despair to hope by turning his eyes toward God’s temple
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:4 says, 'I am cast out of thy sight; yet I will look again toward thy holy temple,' indicating a hopeful turning to God.

questions.question: What cultural or historical context helps explain Jonah’s vow to sacrifice in Jonah 2:9?
options: Sacrificial vows were a common Near Eastern act of thanksgiving and covenant
Sacrifices were forbidden in Israel at the time
Jonah was a priest required to sacrifice daily
Sacrifices were only offered during festivals
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrificial vows were a common Near Eastern act of thanksgiving and covenant
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, making sacrificial vows as a form of thanksgiving and covenant fidelity was common, reflected in Jonah 2:9.

theological.title: Jonah Chapter 2 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jonah Chapter 2 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jonah's prayer from inside the fish's belly primarily demonstrate about God's nature?
options: God is attentive and hears the prayers of the afflicted
questions.correctAnswer: God is attentive and hears the prayers of the afflicted
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:2 shows that Jonah cried out to the LORD in affliction and God heard his voice, demonstrating God's attribute of being attentive to the prayers of the afflicted.

questions.question: Which doctrine is highlighted by Jonah’s statement in verse 9 about sacrifice and salvation?
options: Salvation is based on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is of the LORD
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 states 'Salvation is of the LORD,' affirming the doctrine that salvation is by God's sovereign grace, not by human effort or ritual alone.

questions.question: How does Jonah’s experience in the 'belly of hell' (verse 2) foreshadow New Testament teachings about Christ’s descent and resurrection?
options: It typifies Christ’s descent into death and resurrection unto life
It refers only to Jonah and has no Christological connection
It predicts the destruction of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It typifies Christ’s descent into death and resurrection unto life
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:2’s reference to crying out from the belly of hell prefigures Christ’s descent to the dead and resurrection, as in 1 Peter 3:19 and Acts 2:27, showing typology between Jonah’s deliverance and Christ’s victory over death.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in Jonah 2:6 where God 'brought up my life from corruption'?
options: God's power to save and preserve life
questions.correctAnswer: God's power to save and preserve life
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:6 reveals God's power to rescue from death and corruption, highlighting His attribute as the giver and preserver of life, consistent with Psalm 103:4.

questions.question: According to Jonah 2:4, what does Jonah’s declaration about looking toward God’s holy temple reveal about the nature of prayer and hope?
options: Even in despair, the believer turns to God’s presence as the source of hope
Prayer is only effective in the temple building
Hope is lost once cast out of God's sight
questions.correctAnswer: Even in despair, the believer turns to God’s presence as the source of hope
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:4 shows Jonah’s resolve to look toward God’s holy temple despite feeling cast out, revealing that prayer and hope are directed toward God's presence rather than physical circumstances.

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing Jonah 2:5 and Jonah 2:6 about Jonah’s experience underwater?
options: The doctrine of God’s deliverance from death and judgment
The futility of human efforts under trial
The inevitability of corruption without God
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of God’s deliverance from death and judgment
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:5 describes Jonah surrounded by waters and weeds as a symbol of death’s grasp, while 2:6 speaks of God bringing him up from corruption, together teaching God’s power to deliver from death and judgment.

questions.question: What does Jonah 2:8 teach about the consequences of following 'lying vanities' in relation to God's mercy?
options: Those who trust falsehood forsake their own mercy
Lying vanities lead to God’s mercy
Mercy is independent of human faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Those who trust falsehood forsake their own mercy
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:8 teaches that trusting in falsehood or idols results in abandoning one's own mercy, emphasizing the biblical theme that true mercy comes only from God.

questions.question: How does Jonah’s prayer (verse 7) illustrate the doctrine of sanctification through remembrance of God in affliction?
options: Remembering God rekindles the soul and directs prayer to His holy temple
questions.correctAnswer: Remembering God rekindles the soul and directs prayer to His holy temple
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 shows that when Jonah's soul fainted, he remembered the LORD and his prayer reached God's holy temple, highlighting sanctification as a spiritual renewal by recalling God in affliction.

questions.question: What narrative significance does the LORD’s command to the fish in Jonah 2:10 have in the broader redemptive story of Scripture?
options: It depicts God’s sovereign control over creation to fulfill His redemptive purposes
It shows the fish as an independent agent
It focuses on natural events without divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: It depicts God’s sovereign control over creation to fulfill His redemptive purposes
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:10 reveals God’s sovereign authority over creation by commanding the fish to release Jonah, reflecting the biblical theme of divine control over nature to accomplish salvation history, as seen in Genesis 1.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Jonah’s deliverance was mere luck without divine intervention. What does Jonah 2:1-10 actually teach about God’s involvement in deliverance?
options: God actively hears prayer and commands nature to save Jonah
Jonah escaped by his own strength
The fish acted on instinct without God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: God actively hears prayer and commands nature to save Jonah
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:1-10 documents Jonah’s prayer to God and the LORD’s command to the fish to vomit him out, affirming divine involvement in deliverance rather than chance, consistent with Psalm 34:17.

questions.question: What combined theological truth do Jonah 2:3 and Jonah 2:5 convey about human helplessness and God’s sovereignty in salvation?
options: Humans are overwhelmed by sin and death, but God’s sovereign power surrounds and rescues
Humans can save themselves from the depths
God abandons those overwhelmed by trials
Nature operates independently from God’s will
questions.correctAnswer: Humans are overwhelmed by sin and death, but God’s sovereign power surrounds and rescues
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:3 depicts being surrounded by floods and waves, and 2:5 describes being enveloped by waters and weeds, together illustrating human helplessness; yet God’s sovereignty is implied in Jonah’s survival and eventual salvation.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated in Jonah 2:7 when Jonah’s prayer 'came in unto thee, into thine holy temple'?
options: God’s accessibility and willingness to receive prayers
questions.correctAnswer: God’s accessibility and willingness to receive prayers
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:7 shows that even in deep distress, Jonah’s prayer reaches God's holy temple, revealing God as accessible and receptive to the prayers of His people, as also seen in Psalm 65:2.

questions.question: What does Jonah’s vow to 'pay that that I have vowed' in Jonah 2:9 reveal about the relationship between human response and divine salvation?
options: Salvation prompts grateful obedience and fulfillment of vows
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation prompts grateful obedience and fulfillment of vows
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:9 indicates that upon recognizing salvation as from the LORD, Jonah commits to fulfilling his vows, teaching that salvation leads to thankful obedience without implying salvation is earned by it.

questions.question: How does Jonah 2:1-2 illustrate the doctrine of human sinfulness and God’s mercy in the context of affliction?
options: Despite Jonah’s sinful flight, God hears and shows mercy when he cries out
Human sin makes God deaf to prayer
God’s mercy is automatic regardless of repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Despite Jonah’s sinful flight, God hears and shows mercy when he cries out
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:1-2 shows Jonah praying from the fish’s belly after fleeing God’s command, yet God hears his cry, illustrating that God’s mercy extends even to sinners who repent amid affliction.

questions.question: What does the metaphor of 'the earth with her bars was about me for ever' in Jonah 2:6 teach about the finality of death and God’s power over it?
options: Death seems final and imprisoning, but God can rescue from it
Death is the absolute end with no hope
Bars refer to physical imprisonment only
questions.correctAnswer: Death seems final and imprisoning, but God can rescue from it
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:6 uses the earth’s bars as a metaphor for the finality of death, yet the verse concludes with God bringing Jonah back from corruption, teaching God's power to overcome death’s finality, paralleling Hebrews 2:14.
